title: Evictor hinge + memory migration hotpatch for tensor-pool fragmentation and KV-index drift
creator: Evan Patel
description: Production customer escalation affecting Hosted and Dedicated customers: repeated GPU OOMs on long-running sessions caused by tensor-pool fragmentation combined with KV cache index drift. This ticket tracks a small, low-risk hotpatch that introduces an "evictor hinge" to smooth eviction timing and a controlled memory migration path to defragment active tensor arenas without full session eviction.
incident_summary: Over the last 48 hours multiple customers reported degraded throughput and intermittent OOMs during high-concurrency inference. Pattern: sustained prefix-heavy workloads cause tensor allocation fragmentation; concurrent KV cache snapshot writes race with the compactor and left stale index pointers. Result: allocator unable to find contiguous blocks for large kv/tensor allocations, triggering GPU OOMs and session termination for both Hosted and Dedicated deployments.
reproduction_steps: Simulate 500 concurrent streaming generation sessions with avg prompt length 1.2k tokens and hot prefix reuse pattern (reuse ratio ~70%)
Run workload on 48GB A100-equivalent node with enabled KV snapshotting every 30s
Observe tensor-pool fragmentation increase in /metrics/tensor_arena_free_contiguous and KV index mismatch logs in runtime.log
Trigger allocation for 32k context continuation — observe allocation failure and subsequent OOM in dmesg and runtime trace
root_cause: Two-fold: (1) a defragmentation blind spot in the tensor arena allocator that delayed coalescing of small freed blocks under certain allocation patterns, and (2) a race between KV snapshot compaction and the eviction journal which produced transient stale pointers that prevented proper spill-to-host behavior. Together these starved contiguous allocation paths and escalated into OOMs.
mitigations_taken: Rolled target-specific throttles for affected customers to reduce concurrent warm-prefix sessions (hosted routing policy override)
Deployed a small runtime config (runtime-1.24-canary) that forces eager small-block coalescing on nodes with >60% fragmentation
Enabled emergency KV compactor backoff when eviction latency >120ms to prevent snapshot-induced pointer churn
Temporarily increased swapback timeout and allowed graceful session slow-down instead of hard-oom for Dedicated customers as a short-term failover
long_term_fix: Implement an allocator migration layer that performs background page-level compaction with lease-based session pinning, and rewrite KV snapshot path to be strictly append-only followed by atomic swap of the index pointer to remove transient stale pointer windows. Add stronger unit/integration tests that model high-prefix reuse workloads.
rollout_plan: Canary: runtime-1.24-hotpatch on 5% of Hosted fleet + two Dedicated clusters (staging replica) - 24h watch
If no regressions: ramp to 25% after 24h and run internal synthetic workload for 6h
Roll to 75% over next 12h while monitoring evictor hinge metrics
Post-rollout: enable automatic defrag job on remainder of fleet and schedule final opt-in for Private deployments during maintenance windows (customers notified)
Rollback criteria: increase in tail-latency >15% or spike in allocation retries metric above baseline +10%
monitoring_and_metrics: SLO check: session_restarts_per_min (aim <= 0.1 for affected clusters)
stakeholders: Dr. Maria Chen - Applied ML (allocator expert)
tests: regression: ensure no functional change to streaming latency under 5% delta
follow_up_tasks: ENG-900000: migrate allocator to page-level compactor (epic)
DOC-425: update operator runbook for evictor hinge behavior
OBS-301: add pre-mortem tests to CI that mimic customer prefix-heavy patterns
notes: This hotpatch is intentionally conservative: it adds a time-windowed evictor hinge that spaces eviction wakeups to allow compaction to complete and a memory migration path that copies large allocations into newly-coalesced ranges when safe. The patch was pair-reviewed by allocator and kvcache engineers. Customer Success notified affected accounts; two dedicated customers accepted scheduled maintenance for a full rollback if needed. Post-release we should perform a focused postmortem and update the runbook with exact rollback and customer communication templates.
